overview: The Czech Benoni move order with a King's Indian bishop: White has c4, d5, e4 and Nc3 against ...c5, ...e5, ...d6 and ...g6/...Bg7. The centre is locked, White has more space and Black plays ...O-O, ...Nbd7 and the ...f5 break; Black is cramped but resilient.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the centre closed and use the extra space
Develop Nge2/g3 or Be2 and Bg5, castle kingside
Prepare f4 or a queenside break with b4

black_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight to c5 or e8-f6

typical_structures.structure: Black bishop g7 hemmed in by e5, White dark squares weak after f4

character.notes: A closed, manoeuvring middlegame where Black is cramped but short of weaknesses; sharper only once ...f5 is played.

soundness.notes: Sound, though Black has the passive side.

structure.notes: Pawns on c4/d5/e4 against c5/d6/e5 are locked.

approach.notes: A regular, if less common, Benoni set-up.

level.notes: Both sides need to find plans in a locked position; little forcing theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Four Pawns / f4 setups
sublines_that_differ.how: White plays f4 at once and the game turns sharper and more tactical.

character.reason: Black is cramped but resilient and the locked centre gives few ways to lose quickly.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: Black's passive set-up is accepted as playable.

structure.reason: The d5/e4 and c5/d6/e5 pawns lock the centre and play moves to the wings.

approach.reason: A recognised Benoni set-up that is played less often than the main lines.

level.reason: The plans are clear but need positional judgement rather than memorised lines.

plans.reason: White holds the space and Black's bishops are hemmed in by their own pawns.
